justification: The agents looked at both schemas (S003, S012) and glanced at a few per-ticker sentiment aggregates (S014, S015, S057, S058). The attempt to get firm-level summary statistics failed because STDDEV is not supported (S006), and the agent never retried with another function. It simply assumed mean 0 and sd 1 (S008). It never checked the distribution of avg_sentiment for news_count>=5, which is the range that decides whether the 0.60 and -0.20 cutoffs ever fire. S035 was an undated query of whole-market daily averages, and the agent misread its output as a trailing 30-day range (S036).

No candidate rule was ever tested against ret_fwd_1 in aggregate; the audit shows training_queries_using_ret_fwd_1 is empty. The only checks were pass counts (117 and 45 over the window in S005/S007; 6 and 2 on 2023-06-30 in S027/S028/S048/S050). test_complex_condition did print per-firm ret_fwd_1, but those values were ignored: DPZ was flagged SELL and returned +17.7%, and nobody commented. The Reflector never looked at realized returns.

The fundamental thresholds (bm>1.15, mom12m>0.73, mve<1.11) are the prompt's first example, copied word for word, and the SELL side is just the same numbers with the signs flipped. avg_sentiment>0.60 and news_count>=5 also come from the prompt's examples. -0.20 has no source in any tool output. The audit puts the copied share at 56%. No threshold changed after any tool result.

Tools were called 22 times, but many calls were redundant: the schema was fetched 6 times and the same 2023-06-30 condition was tested repeatedly (S027/S028 and again in S048/S050). The STDDEV error was never recovered. S035 ran without a date filter. No tool result changed any conclusion: the rule is identical from S008 to S073. The evaluator's tool calls at S068-S072 did execute the rule correctly.

The rule joins the fundamental and sentiment legs with OR, and the only reason given is that it is 'more comprehensive' (S039). Nobody checked how often the two signals overlap or whether OR beats AND. The sentiment BUY leg is effectively dead: it matched 0 firms on the decision date and 2 of 852 ticker-months in training. That leaves BUY entirely fundamental, and nobody noticed.

Precedence is explicit with parentheses, the rule uses only available variables, and BUY and SELL are disjoint and both non-empty on the decision date (audit: BUY 17, SELL 10, overlap 0). One caveat: the sentiment BUY leg is empty, so BUY comes from fundamentals alone.

During training, S035 queried the whole ravenpack table without a date filter and got back rows dated up to 2025-12-31. The agent quoted those rows in its summary (S036). They did not change any threshold, but it is still an excursion beyond the window. All other training queries stayed inside the window, and the evaluation used no forward returns.
The final step applied rulebook v2.2 exactly as written and output explicit thresholds. It tested each leg on 2024-07-31.

The rationale is generic textbook value/momentum/size language. Some claims have no support: S016 says high sentiment coincides with higher news counts without any analysis. S036 calls whole-market daily averages a trailing 30-day sentiment range of 0.04-0.19. mve<1.11 is described as 'smaller firm size' even though it lets in almost the whole universe. The rationale also ignores the DPZ counterexample.

The agent checked the schemas (S003, S012) and computed means and variances of the z-scores (S007). It never looked at tails or quantiles near its chosen cutoffs (±1.2, 0.7, sentiment 0.5–0.7). Sentiment exploration amounted to 5 printed rows from one month, partly before the training window (S014, S038), plus June 2023, which is outside the window (S063). It never checked how often avg_sentiment exceeds 0.7 with five or more stories, so it missed that the sentiment BUY leg almost never fires.

Only one training query used ret_fwd_1 (S038). It returned 5 rows of July 2023 ticker averages, which says nothing about any candidate rule, and the agent drew only a vague 'returns generally negative' remark from it (S039). No BUY-vs-SELL return or hit-rate comparison was ever run. test_complex_condition and test_sentiment_condition were never used during training. Thresholds changed (0.6→0.7, 0.2→0.3) with no outcome evidence.

Every threshold is a round number that was nudged without data. Fundamentals went from 1.0/0.5 to 1.2/0.7 with no tool output behind the change (S032). Sentiment went from 0.6/0.2 to 0.7/0.3, then extra 0.5/7 and 0.4/7 legs were added (S039, S042). The abs≤3 caps come from the prompt's warning. news_count>=5 and avg_sentiment>0.5 match prompt examples (per the audit). None of the cutoffs traces to a tool result.

The agent hit the same missing STDDEV function three times (S005, S028, S051) and then tried STDEV (S053), even though it had already found a working variance formula in S007. Queries were repeated (S026/S029, S013/S061). The S027 query has an operator-precedence bug: the date filter attaches only to the last OR clause, so it scanned the whole table. Nobody noticed. The rule-testing tools were used only at evaluation, and the S076 result that 0 names pass the sentiment BUY condition was ignored. Overall, the tools did not change any conclusion.

In iteration 1 the Reflector joined the fundamental and sentiment rules with OR (S018). In iteration 2 it switched to AND (S042) with no data showing how the two signals interact. The switch is simply asserted ('strong buy signals'). The rule does combine both domains, but the structure is not argued from evidence.

The rule is fully parenthesised, uses only available variables, and BUY and SELL do not overlap. On the decision date, however, BUY is empty: the sentiment BUY leg passes 0 names (S076), so the unified BUY passes 0. SELL passes only 2. The rule is executable but has an empty side.

Most training queries stayed inside the training window and the evaluation used no returns. However, S027/S030 actually scanned the whole firms table, including rows dated after the decision date, because of the precedence bug. It was only a count of feature extremes, but it is an undated excursion. S063 queried June 2023 sentiment, which is before the window (not future data). The audit did not flag look-ahead. This counts as a minor excursion.

The evaluator copied rulebook v3.1 word for word into the final strategy, with explicit thresholds (S078). It tested every component on the decision date (S073–S077). It did not respond to the empty sentiment BUY result, but it did not rewrite the rule either.

The rationale is generic ('minimizes the risk of false signals', 'enhances robustness') and not backed by any tool output. S039 claims returns were 'generally negative' based on 5 rows. S056 assumes std = 1 after failing to compute it, even though S007 had already shown variances of 1.0/0.99/0.97. The small-cap BUY leg is justified by takeover and growth stories with no data behind them. Nothing directly contradicts the rule, but the claims are unsupported.
